statement: On cold school days New York City public-school absence is higher than on other school days of the same week of the year, as the open triad temperature - asthma - school attendance in the System Public Graph implies; the graph holds no finding that links temperature to school attendance directly.

graph_evidence.concepts: temperature family (hot, temperature, air temperature) - asthma
graph_evidence.direction: + for heat in the hot season and + for cold in the cold season; the 32 positive and 8 negative rows mix both, and include heaters and exhaled temperature
graph_evidence.summary: cold (5th percentile of temperature) and childhood asthma hospitalisation, RR 1.64 (1.06-2.54) on days with lower PM2.5, Hefei 2013-2016; also low temperature RR 1.20 (1.15-1.26), Lanzhou (PMID 39251927), and 1.10 (1.05-1.15) in adults, Hong Kong (PMID 36240934)

children with asthma had 2.21 (1.41-3.01) more days absent per year than matched children without asthma, Rochester, Minnesota (abstract read; the relationship record lists 31 studies but the API returns one finding)
no direct finding in the graph for hot, temperature, air temperature, surface temperature, heat wave or urban heat island with school attendance (two findings from two studies with absenteeism)

literature.citation: Keivabu RC. Temperature and school absences: evidence from England. Population and Environment 2024
literature.finding: hot days increase absences in English schools; cold days show no substantive effect. Not in the graph. Read as a search summary only, not the paper.

composition.method: kit.bridge.compose, log RR(absence) = share x log RR(asthma exacerbation), 20000 draws, seed 1

exponent.meaning: share of pupil absences attributable to asthma = prevalence U(0.08, 0.15) x excess days 2.21 (1.41-3.01) / mean days absent U(13, 20); prevalence and mean days absent are the registrant's assumptions, not graph findings

discrimination.advice: the test cannot separate the chain from no effect; find a larger contrast or a more precise endpoint

prediction.magnitude: Composed through asthma alone: absence ratio 1.0073 (95% interval 1.0008 to 1.0173). With an expected standard error near 0.016 on the log scale the test cannot separate this size from no effect (D = 0.23, below 4). The registrant expects the direct association to be larger than the chain, between 1.00 and 1.08, because temperature can affect attendance by routes other than asthma.
prediction.support_if: the absence ratio for exposed days is above 1 and its 95% interval (Newey-West) excludes 1. The direction composed from the triad is then confirmed. Whether the interval contains the composed interval is reported as a second, registered quantity (the share of the association that the asthma path can account for = composed log ratio / city log ratio).
prediction.refute_if: the absence ratio is below 1 and its 95% interval excludes 1.

plan: Unit: school day, citywide, school years 2006-07 to 2018-19. Outcome: log(sum of absent / sum of enrolled) over all schools by date, from NYC Open Data daily attendance by school (xwxx-rnki, wpqj-3buw, pffu-gbfi, 3y5p-x48f, x3bb-kg5j), aggregated in SoQL. Exclusions fixed now: weekends; days whose citywide enrolment is below 80% of that school year's median; days with an absence rate above 30%. Arm: school days in December, January and February. Exposure: Central Park TMAX <= 0.0 C on the same day (NOAA GHCN-Daily USW00094728). Model: OLS of the log absence rate on the exposure indicator with fixed effects for school year, day of week and ISO week of the year, and indicators for precipitation >= 10 mm, and snowfall > 0 on the same or the previous day, for a school day next to a weekday without school, and for the last five school days of the school year. Standard errors Newey-West with 5 lags. Estimate: exp(coefficient) with its 95% interval. Secondary, not deciding: exposure on any of lags 0 to 2; a linear term per 5 C of TMAX within the arm; the hot arm without the last two weeks of June; the same model on the school-level medians is not planned.
alternatives: Temperature affects attendance directly (discomfort, travel, classrooms without air conditioning, families' choices), not through asthma; a ratio far above the composed interval indicates this.

Calendar: late June is hot and attendance falls at the end of the year; winter cold coincides with influenza season and snow. Week-of-year and school-year effects and the snow indicator address this in part; influenza is not controlled.
Citywide aggregation hides schools that close or report late on extreme days; the exclusions address this in part.
The asthma links come from hospital admissions in Hong Kong, Hefei, Lanzhou and Florida and from 92 children in Minnesota; none is a New York school population.
disclosure: No attendance data had been queried by this project before registration (no file for these datasets in data/cache/socrata; only the catalog's column names were read). The Central Park temperature series had been used by earlier claims, and the counts of exposed days (116 of 843 hot-season weekdays, 145 of 838 cold-season weekdays) were computed from it before registration. The registrant knows in general that New York attendance falls in late June and on snow days. A web search summary of Keivabu 2024 was read before registration.
